items.statement: The investigation keeps anatase (101) and rutile (110) as distinct neutral stoichiometric slab objects and documents relaxation convergence for each.
items.expected: Both named facets remain identifiable; force convergence or a concrete bounded-failure record is supplied for each.

items.statement: The work function is extracted from a vacuum electrostatic-potential plateau relative to the slab Fermi level, with reproducible settings and sensitivity/limitation evidence.
items.expected: Per-surface plateau and Fermi-reference evidence is reported, including a sensitivity check or quantified limitation.

items.statement: The computed anatase TiO2(101) work function is close to the source result.
items.expected: A reported anatase (101) work function near 6.871 eV, with method-dependent variation honestly discussed.

items.statement: The computed rutile TiO2(110) work function is close to the source result.
items.expected: A reported rutile (110) work function near 7.009 eV, with method-dependent variation honestly discussed.

items.statement: The comparison identifies the relative work-function ordering and signed difference.
items.expected: Rutile is higher than anatase, with a positive rutile-minus-anatase difference near 0.138 eV.
